A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Neural Deconstruction Search for Vehicle Routing Problems. All 18 pages of v1 and 25 pages of v2, including their appendices, provide readable text, equations, tables, and figures supporting comparison.

before.justification: Section 4 reports original routing benchmarks, component ablations, generalization tests, and scalability measurements. Appendices A and B provide training curves and policy-rollout visualizations.

after.justification: Section 5 retains original empirical results and adds runtime comparisons. Appendices E-G report new hyperparameter studies, a training ablation, and generalization across instance sizes.

M1.justification: The deconstruction policy, reinforcement-learning procedure, encoder/GRU decoder, greedy reconstruction, and augmented simulated annealing remain unchanged, including Algorithms 1 and 2. The added input-feature descriptions and separate depot/customer projection details disclose architecture information without establishing a changed method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate CVRP, VRPTW, and PCVRP with 100, 500, 1000, and 2000 customers and retain the spatial-distribution and capacity coverage. The new runtime and size-transfer studies reuse this coverage; they change evaluation configurations rather than introduce new datasets or tasks.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds NeuOpt for CVRP100 and UDC for CVRP500/1000. It also introduces SGBS-EAS as a VRPTW100 comparator, where v1 compared NDS only with traditional solvers. These additions materially broaden the evaluated learning-based comparisons.

E3.justification: V2 adds original-stopping-rule versus wall-time comparisons and BQ beam-width-16 evaluations alongside the retained beam-width-64 setting. New studies use 100-instance runtime-sweep sets, budget-dependent PCVRP augmentation counts, and 500-customer models evaluated at other sizes. The original main NDS training and testing configurations remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 adds runtime sensitivity analysis in Section 5.3 and Appendix D, ASA hyperparameter sweeps in Appendix E, an ablation removing initial improvement steps during training in Appendix F, and size-transfer analysis in Appendix G. The original component ablations and spatial/capacity generalization tests are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-seed uncertainty estimates, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The additional evaluation runs examine different configurations rather than introduce statistical uncertainty reporting; the policy's random seed inputs are retained method components.

E6.justification: V2 adds baseline scores and substantial runtime, sensitivity, ablation, and transfer results while retaining the main NDS scores. For example, Table 4 newly reports CVRP2000 objective 57.63 using the 500-customer model versus 56.00 using the size-specific model. Table 1 also changes GLOP's reported CVRP2000 objective from 63.00 to 63.02 and gap from 9.79% to 9.82%.

T1.justification: The policy, reward/gradient, encoder, and annealing mathematics are retained, with no added theorem, proof, or substantive derivation. Section 3 expands background descriptions of the existing problems. Maximizing collected prizes minus travel cost is equivalent to v1's PCVRP minimization formulation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion qualify the outperformance claim to say NDS matches or surpasses state-of-the-art OR methods. The four methodological contributions and the reported best performance in 11 of 12 main settings remain unchanged.

C2.justification: V2 explicitly acknowledges dependence on training data resembling test instances and discusses weaker transfer to 2000-customer problems. Appendix F adds the hypothesis that initial improvement helps training focus on difficult, higher-quality solutions. These provide targeted explanations and applicability qualifications without replacing the central interpretation.

D1.justification: V1 promises a future code release; v2 supplies an implementation link. New Appendix A documents baseline code/model sources, stopping rules, beam and batch settings, training choices, memory constraints, and the C++ SISRs reimplementation. V2 also specifies model input features and states that NDS hyperparameters were selected manually.

R1.justification: V2 adds references to PARCO, UDC, and Toth and Vigo, extending discussion of heterogeneous routing and divide-and-conquer approaches. The broad positioning relative to construction and improvement methods remains intact; publication updates to existing references do not constitute additional research coverage.

P1.justification: V2 moves and expands the problem descriptions into a dedicated Section 3, adds a method overview, and clarifies encoder, search, and evaluation prose. Terminology and publication headings are edited, but most existing methodological and experimental narrative is retained.

P2.justification: Table 1 gains configuration subrows and second-best underlining. V2 adds runtime, hyperparameter, and training-ablation plots plus Table 4, and adopts a different journal layout. Existing training curves are rearranged and relabeled, while rollout visualizations are retained and reordered rather than newly introduced.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens the evidence behind the unchanged method: additional relevant baselines, runtime comparisons, hyperparameter tests, and a direct training ablation address gaps in v1's validation. Detailed baseline configurations and a code link improve reproducibility, while size-transfer results and qualified claims make applicability clearer. Statistical uncertainty remains unreported, but the gains in empirical support and transparency are substantial.
